Fwiw, while it is nice if the test suite runs with a pool enabled I don't think it is a requirement to get this merged. The test suite is rather special after all. Nevertheless it might also show us bugs in the implementation.

Not sure what the plan was, but are we going to document that users cannot test their apps when connection pooling is enabled? They can encounter the same issues.

Some failures are really suspicious, e.g. `backends.tests.BackendTestCase.test_is_usable_after_database_disconnects`:
```
  File "/django/tests/backends/tests.py", line 486, in test_is_usable_after_database_disconnects
    self.assertFalse(connection.is_usable())
AssertionError: True is not false
```

Why connection is usable after `_close()`? Maybe I'm missing something.

Ah that is because the connection isn't closed on `close` but only returned to the pool. I guess we really have to set `self.connection` to `None` afterwards since we no longer own it and adjust the remaining code to handle `None` there then (eg in `is_usable`)

So, I had some time and managed to get the testsuite passing with pooling enabled. During that I discovered one bug in the implementation that we should discuss (see below). I opened a PR against this PR, see https://github.com/sarahboyce/django/pull/10 for the details.

The code looks clean imo but there are a few things that might need some improving (note that by default the whole testsuite does not run under pooling, so the issues don't show up and even when they show up, this is basically Django testing transaction behavior. Endusers will probably never see that).

I am getting:
> rolling back returned connection: <psycopg.Connection [INTRANS] (user=florian database=test_django_test_1) at 0x7f61920c5690>

for the following two tests:
* `test_hooks_cleared_on_reconnect`
* `test_atomic_prevents_queries_in_broken_transaction_after_client_close`

Both tests explicitly close the connection (and as such return it to the pool) while a transaction is active. So the warning is expected and the only thing I can think of is using filterwarnings to filter out those pgpool warnings here. But as said above I don't think this is necessary since that is not a default configuration we run the tests against.

I had the same warning for `test_skip_class_unless_db_feature` but I was able to fix it via https://github.com/sarahboyce/django/pull/10/commits/962566c4b62ef48fbdae1cb2ff75ed69147d186c -- this wouldn't hurt in current main either, @felixxm do you want an extra cleanup PR for that one or can we just keep it as extra commit in this PR?

`test_atomic_prevents_queries_in_broken_transaction_after_client_close` exposed one bug. Because we set `connection = None` in `_close` after we returned the connection to the pool (to ensure we do not use it…), we were able to reopen a connection inside an atomic. Essentially this means that
```py
        with transaction.atomic():
            Reporter.objects.create(first_name="Archibald", last_name="Haddock")
            connection.close()
            # The connection is closed and the transaction is marked as
            # needing rollback. This will raise an InterfaceError on databases
            # that refuse to create cursors on closed connections (PostgreSQL)
            # and a TransactionManagementError on other databases.
            with self.assertRaises(Error):
                Reporter.objects.create(first_name="Cuthbert", last_name="Calculus")
```
no longer raises. Without pooling `self.connection` is not `None` and as such opening a new cursor raises. I was able to fix this in `ensure_connection` by adding:
```
        if self.in_atomic_block and self.closed_in_transaction:
            raise ProgrammingError("Cannot open a new connection in an atomic block.")
```
Basically use the existing hints to determine if we closed inside a transaction and error out. I am wondering if it would make sense to move this solely into the postgres backend. In the end though the check is not *wrong* but instead of relying on the database adapter to throw errors for closed connections we error out realy -- sounds okay?

I had to rewrite a few postgres tests to use a non-pooling connection because the pool doesn't tolerate changes to the settings dict like presented (see https://github.com/sarahboyce/django/pull/10/commits/bbd5c5db2c3523b1e0b02e3242ae5c1aa5d2c34d for details). There might be some ways to rewrite them in a pooling way, this way we can reuse the existing tests to test whether timezones & assume_role work instead of adding new ones. I don't have strong feeling either way though.

I will do some manual testing against a simple app, but so far so good.

Hi! 
First of all, thanks for all the work that's being done on this.

I'm looking to use this thread pool in the future, in combination with `gevent`. After some local testing, I found out the current solution opens a new threadpool on every new request, which for my use case is the same as using persistent connections.

Is this something that can/will be considered in the requirements? Is this threadpool even something that can be used with gevent in the first place?

Thank you :pray:

As far as I know Django doesn't support `gevent` officially. So no, this is not something I would consider, I have no idea how `gevent` works. That said if the existing thread locals do work, I am kinda surprised since I am not doing anything magic (I think).
